newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto-Dominion Bank profit up, but stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Toronto-Dominion Bank profit up, but stock falls.

text.p: Toronto-Dominion Bank's first-quarter earnings beat analysts' expectations on Thursday, but its shares declined along with other bank stocks.

Canada's fifth biggest bank said that its profit for the first quarter ended Jan. 31 rose to C$256 million ($188 million) or C83 cents (61 cents) a share from C$214 million ($157 million) or C70 cents (51 cents) a share a year earlier.
The results topped analysts' expectations by about C2 cents. Earlier this week, Canada's third and fourth biggest banks, Bank of Montreal and Bank of Nova Scotia, also bested analysts' forecasts.
Toronto-Dominion said its earnings gain was driven by strength in residential mortgages and personal lending, retail brokerage, mutual funds and corporate and investment banking.
Its return on equity improved to 16.4 percent for the quarter from 15.2 percent in the previous year.

But Toronto-Dominion stock fell C70 cents to C$38.80 in Toronto on Thursday as interest-rate sensitive stocks declined after U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan said on Wednesday that the Fed may need to raise interest rates to pre-empt a rise in inflation.

Toronto-Dominion said it raised its 1997 loan loss provision to C$160 million ($117.6 million) from C$152 million ($111.8 million) in 1996 and charged C$40 million ($29.4 million) of the loss provision to the first quarter.
Toronto-Dominion said net problem loans increased to C$514 million ($380 million) at Jan. 31 from C$344 million ($253 million) at Oct. 31, 1996.
The bank said the rise in loan loss provisions was due mainly to lower credit quality in loans to the forestry sector.
